paper_title: Results of a Search for Paraphotons with Intense X-ray Beams at SPring-8
notes: Light-Shining-through-a-Wall paraphoton (dark photon) search at the BL19LXU X-ray beamline, SPring-8. Headline result (abstract, Eq. 3, and conclusion): kinetic mixing chi < 8.06e-5 (95% C.L.) for 0.04 eV < m_gamma' < 26 keV, reported here as two points spanning that stated flat mass range (0.04 eV to 26000 eV). The paper reports the mixing chi directly in the canonical -(chi/2) F F' convention, so no conversion is needed. Fig. 4 (limit.eps in the e-print) shows the combined 'our experiment' curve: an oscillating LSW limit that rises steeply toward chi=1 below ~0.05 eV (chi ~ m^-2 in the low-mass region) and forms a plateau; I vector-parsed the blue polyline (calibration x: 538px=1e-4 eV, 204.5px/decade; y: log10(chi)=(py-1514)/157.75), giving a plateau median ~3.9e-5 with worst-case spikes up to ~8e-5. The 8.06e-5 headline is the single worst point chi_worst=8.01e-5 at 1.39 eV plus a +0.52% systematic, used as a conservative blanket bound over the whole 0.04 eV-26 keV range. I report the flat headline value the paper emphasizes; the plateau minimum (~4e-5) differs by a factor <2. Not a dark-matter search, so no density rescaling (dm_density_assumed null).
